scope: Visual intent clarification. Schematics are interpretations, not reference screenshots or a redesigned app.

items.title: Avatar & identity
items.user: The Muse is an interactive avatar … I am not able to click on the agent itself.
items.observed: The reference shows a small avatar in the rail and a larger avatar, name, status and controls in the agent panel.
items.mismatch: The prototype substitutes a wordmark and an invented Atlas card for the agent identity and entry point.
items.proposal: Use the avatar as an entry point to the agent workspace. Agree its appearance and motion separately; keep the companion name undecided.
items.unknown: Exact opening transition, animation and whether the avatar is 3D remain unverified.
items.check: Demonstrate the avatar at rest and on selection, then show where the user lands. Obtain visual agreement before choosing artwork.

items.title: Collapsible navigation
items.user: There is one collapsible sidebar … ideas, goals … search button and chat … feed.
items.observed: The Feed frame has a narrow icon rail, avatar and a toggle. The video and transcript establish Chat, Feed, Ideas and Goals; library is discussed later.
items.mismatch: The prototype omits destinations and does not reproduce the collapse interaction the user expects.
items.proposal: Keep navigation distinct from agent details. Show an icon rail and a labelled expanded state; preserve the selected destination when toggling.
items.unknown: Expanded width, exact label order, icon artwork and transition need reference confirmation. This map's expanded rail is a proposal.
items.check: Show collapsed and expanded states beside their reference, including the active destination and return to chat.

items.title: Agent & document workspace
items.user: It is not open for Atlas. It is just open for my work … memory or soul … browser … computer use.
items.observed: An agent panel has avatar, status, tabs, Edit and SOUL/MEMORY cards. A larger adjacent workspace opens MEMORY.md or SOUL.md; the SOUL editor has Save and close controls.
items.mismatch: A task evidence drawer was treated as if it also represented the agent's identity, memory and capabilities.
items.proposal: Separate agent information, editable documents and task outputs. Browser/computer access must have their own demonstrated states before implementation.
items.unknown: Browser/computer panel details, tab meanings and unsaved-edit handling still need evidence or an explicit design decision.
items.check: Demonstrate opening each document and returning without losing the conversation. Compare task outputs separately.

items.title: Settings & preferences
items.user: The settings button is also just showing me … agent display name and the appearance. Nothing else.
items.observed: The inspected frames do not establish the complete settings experience. No reference settings layout is claimed here.
items.mismatch: A two-field dialog was presented without first identifying the reference's settings structure and contents.
items.proposal: First capture settings entry, layout and categories. Consider app preferences and agent configuration separately; approve that distinction visually.
items.unknown: Settings layout, full categories, defaults and save behavior are unresolved. Do not invent a finished settings screen.
items.check: Review the settings reference or an explicitly proposed alternative. Theme saving already works in the prototype; the user corrected that complaint.

items.title: Conversation & composer
items.user: It looks similar, but not clean … rather than … a send button … the blue top to send it.
items.observed: The main chat frame establishes the conversation area, narrow rail and separate activity area. Exact send-control states are not yet confirmed.
items.mismatch: The prototype uses its own send treatment and visual spacing. Working submission does not establish reference fidelity.
items.proposal: Compare composer proportions, spacing, message surfaces and send icon together. Demonstrate empty, typing and sending states at normal and wide windows.
items.unknown: Exact icon, dimensions, attachment controls and sending states still require visual confirmation. The blue arrow in this sketch is proposed.
items.check: Compare the same chat state and window size. Verify both the appearance and the available space when another panel is open.
